Figure 1:PyRUA-REAL: Python-based Robot-Use Agents for Robot Exploration and Adaptive Learning.(a) Coding agents iteratively explore, execute,
diagnose, and revise robot programs, retaining rollout experience
as persistent memory and reusable skills. (b) Development-stage improvements in success rate and cycle time, including reset, for stacking, tic-tac-toe, and Hanoi. (c) Real-world success rates aggregated over development attempts for seven agent-free skills. (d) RoboDojo performance compared with eight baselines, measured by success rate averaged equally over five capability groups. (e) The eight real-world tasks include semantic reasoning, precise manipulation, contact-rich manipulation, deformable object manipulation and long-horizon tasks.
Figure 2:PyRUA-REAL develops executable policies through researcher–engineer collaboration and retains facts, memories, and code for reuse. The resulting policy uses live feedback during execution.

Figure 3:Eight real-world tasks. Top row: (a) tic-tac-toe, (b) five-block stacking, (c) Tower of Hanoi, and (d) Ethernet insertion. Bottom row: (e) towel folding, (f) Push T, (g) block sorting, and (h) block storage. Images show scenes recorded during task execution.
